paper_metadata.title: Low-energy semi-coherent interfaces deliver strength-plasticity synergy and softening resistance in a lightweight refractory high-entropy alloy

evidence.section: Abstract

evidence.section: 1 Introduction
evidence.quote: The present study develops a novel TiZrNbV0.6Al0.75 LRHEA through compositional optimization of the previously reported TiZrNbV0.6 system [17].

evidence.section: 2 Experimental
evidence.quote: The TiZrNbV0.6Al0.75 alloy ingot was fabricated via a DHL-1250 vacuum arc melting equipment using high-purity (> 99.9 wt%) constituent metals in a Ti- doped high-purity argon atmosphere. The ingot was remelted at least five times to ensure the chemical homogeneity

evidence.section: 2 Experimental

evidence.section: 3.3 Microstructure evolution during deformation at room temperature

evidence.section: 1 Introduction
evidence.quote: These semi-coherent interfaces exhibit exceptional tolerance for dislocations, effectively prevent dislocation pile-up, while the C14 intermetallics provide significant precipitation strengthening effect.

evidence.section: 4.4 The deformation behavior at room temperature
evidence.quote: the multiple slip in matrix and the semi-coherent interfaces could effectively alleviate strain localization, appreciable plasticity is achieved in the high-strength TiZrNbV0.6Al0.75 LRHEA.

evidence.section: 4.5 The softening resistance at elevated temperatures
evidence.quote: a higher energy barrier must be overcome for atomic migration across the interface, which effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and interface migration at high temperature

evidence.section: 4.5 The softening resistance at elevated temperatures
evidence.quote: the stable existence of the C14 intermetallics plays an important role in pinning grain boundaries and dislocations (Fig. 6D), inhibiting dynamic recrystallization and grain coarsening (Fig. 7A). Therefore, high yield strength and large rET/rRT values are achieved at temperatures higher than 0.6 Tm
